notes: Days of Wonder North America base game only; Europe, USA 1910, Legacy, and other map collections are separate editions and excluded.

The official map transcription retains all 36 city IDs and 98 physical route IDs, including route length/color and parallel identity. `network` also records segment polygons used to place every train piece along each route.

The complete table now has five player zones each for private train cards, private destination tickets, and public remaining trains. The 2–5 player selector hides unused seat zones. Colors in the SVG mark neutral seat templates, not assigned players.

Shared state includes five face-up train cards, train deck/discard, ticket deck, the longest-path bonus card, and five player markers on the score sequence. Market/card graphics are empty position guides, not initialized card contents.

The 2–3 player double-route closure rule, route-level ownership, individual segment occupancy, current turn/action checkpoint, destination-ticket secrecy, final turn trigger, final score and tie state are described in `tableModel`. No legal-move or scoring engine is included.
This is a self-contained asset package only. It is not connected to application rendering, state editing, or save/resume code.

structureEvidence.method: official web rulebook or publisher text
structureEvidence.verifiedStructure: Five face-up train cards; public map with multiple route lengths; 45 trains per player.

structureEvidence.verifiedFacts: 36 North American cities/98 physical routes per the transcribed official map; 0-start scoring track around board edge; score route lengths 1–6 as 1,2,4,7,10,15; 5 face-up train cards; 110 train cards, 33 tickets, 45 trains per player, 5 scoring markers and one longest-path bonus card.
structureEvidence.access: official publisher PDF text and map directly reviewed

assetScope: Complete self-contained Ticket to Ride North America base-game table asset: official route network, route occupancy geometry, player-specific private/public zones, shared card piles, score track, and resumable session-state description. Application consumer integration and rule enforcement are not claimed.

tableModel.sourceEdition: Ticket to Ride North America base game; Days of Wonder 2025 English rules and map

players.seatLayout: neutral schematic; not a fixed printed seating order

shared.trainDrawDeck: remaining train cards after deal and market
shared.destinationTicketDeck: remaining tickets after initial deal and returned tickets at bottom

notes: Returned initial tickets are shuffled and placed at the bottom of the ticket deck.
Do not assume exact randomized card order from counts alone.

board.cities: network.cities, 36 stable IDs with coordinate and label
board.routes: network.routes, 98 stable physical IDs, each with endpoints, printed length/color, and one segment coordinate per train piece

routeClaim.cardColorUsed: one route color or null for unknown
routeClaim.segmentOccupancy: array of length route.length, each element {segmentIndex, trainInstanceId, ownerPlayerId}; a claim fills the entire route in one turn
routeClaim.closedWithoutOwner: boolean for a parallel route closed under the 2–3 player double-route rule

board.parallelRouteRule: In 2- or 3-player games, only one of each parallel double route may be claimed; with more players, one player may not claim both routes in a pair.

trainCardHand.items: array of {instanceId,color}; color may be locomotive

score.track: 0..100 with explicit overflowPoints if a saved value exceeds displayed track

sharedCardState.faceUpMarket: exactly five position records; each current card instance/color or empty during replacement

turnState.actionTaken: one of draw train cards, claim route, draw tickets, or null
turnState.ticketsDrawnThisAction: array of private ticket IDs or null
turnState.ticketsKeptThisAction: array of private ticket IDs or null
turnState.pendingResolution: checkpoint for a partially completed physical action; preserve exact step and do not replay on resume

endState.trigger: At the end of a turn when any player has 0, 1, or 2 trains left; every player, including that player, takes one final turn.
endState.finalTicketStatuses: explicit per-ticket completed/incomplete/unknown values; do not infer from incomplete route ownership data
endState.finalScoreBreakdown: route points, completed/failed tickets, bonus, and final total per player

visibilityRules: Each player’s held destination tickets remain secret until game end.
A player’s train-card hand is kept in that player area; do not expose identity unless explicitly shared.
Route owner and occupied train segments are public.
Unknown card order, ticket status, and route ownership remain unknown; do not infer from remaining inventory.
resumeRequirements: active player, turn number, action phase, and whether one or two cards have been drawn
all five public market slots and pending replacements
train draw/discard piles, including unknown order/count
all player train-card hands with owner-private identity
all player destination tickets with owner-private identity and explicit completion status
all 98 route claim/closure states, each occupied segment and owner
five score marker positions and per-player remaining train counts
ticket-draw keep/return checkpoint and private ticket state
final-turn trigger, remaining final turns, bonus holder/ties, and final scoring breakdown
limitations: This asset represents board/session state; it does not enforce legal actions, compute ticket connectivity, calculate longest route, score actions, or advance turns automatically.
Network layout is a clean schematic transcription of the official North America map; commercial artwork is not copied.

assetCompleteness: Full 2–5 player North America base-game table: 36-city/98-route map, five player hand/ticket/train areas, route ownership and segment state, five-card public market, draw/discard/ticket decks, longest-path bonus, 0–100 score sequence, turn and final-round state.
